items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Don wrote the arrangements for this... We had a meeting... Don did the same thing. He did that for The Rite of Spring... I remember Don coming in. We already did the first part... his lush arrangements made it very successful

ctx.x: Yeah, he arranged that. We had a meeting. He, Creed, and I had a meeting, I remember, at Rockefeller Center, where they had their offices, and we sat up and talked about things we ought to record for the next record. We came up with that. I’m going to tell you: Don wrote the arrangements for this, as well as the Passacaglia. He sat out there in the car at Rudy Van Gelder’s studio and jotted down these parts. I’m telling you. I’ve still got the originals. It’s hardly legible. This guy sat there with a pencil. I…

outside the studio, at Rudy Van Gelder, while we were in warming up and doing all – I’m sure he took a little bit longer. Maybe he was finishing it up there. But he certainly had it in pencil. There was no ink.
